questions.q: Sequestrum is defined as:
opts: Dead, dense, devascularized bone inside abscess
questions.exp: Sequestrum: pathological hallmark of chronic osteomyelitis - dead, dense, devascularized bone inside abscess. (Book p141)

questions.q: Sequestrum is surrounded by:
questions.exp: Surrounded by granulation tissue and involucrum. (Book p141)

questions.q: Microscopy of sequestrum shows:
questions.exp: Microscopically: destruction of haversian system. (Book p141)

questions.q: Coraliform sequestrum is associated with:
questions.exp: Coraliform → Perthe's. (Book p141)

questions.q: Annular/ring sequestrum is seen at:
questions.exp: Annular/ring → amputation stump/pin tract sites. (Book p141)

questions.q: Tubular/diaphyseal sequestrum is characteristic of:
questions.exp: Tubular/diaphyseal → acute pyogenic osteomyelitis. (Book p141)

questions.q: Feathery/flake/coarse sandy sequestrum is seen in:
questions.exp: Feathery/flake/coarse sandy → tuberculosis. (Book p141)

questions.q: Fine sandy sequestrum is characteristic of:
questions.exp: Fine sandy → viral osteomyelitis. (Book p141)

questions.q: Button hole sequestrum occurs:
questions.exp: Button hole → post radiation. (Book p141)

questions.q: Ivory sequestrum is classically associated with:
questions.exp: Ivory → syphilis. (Book p141)

questions.q: X-ray in chronic osteomyelitis shows:
questions.exp: Radiology - X-ray: sequestrum, involucrum, cloaca. (Book p141)

questions.q: Sinogram in chronic osteomyelitis is done by:
opts: Dye injected through sinus - anatomy of sinus tract seen - plan Rx
questions.exp: Sinogram: dye injected through sinus → anatomy of sinus tract seen → plan Rx. (Book p141)

questions.q: Gold standard investigation in chronic osteomyelitis:
questions.exp: Biopsy: gold standard. (Book p141)

questions.q: Initial treatment of chronic osteomyelitis:
questions.exp: Initial: broad spectrum antibiotics, supportive treatment. (Book p141)

questions.q: Definitive treatment of chronic osteomyelitis:
questions.exp: Definitive: surgery. (Book p142)

questions.q: Surgery for chronic osteomyelitis is done under:
questions.exp: Sequence: antibiotic cover → sequestrectomy. (Book p142)

questions.q: Sequestrectomy means:
questions.exp: Sequestrectomy: removal of sequestrum. (Book p142)

questions.q: Curettage in chronic osteomyelitis surgery is done till:
questions.exp: Curettage: till fresh bleed seen - Paprika sign. (Book p142)

questions.q: Debridement of chronic osteomyelitis cavity by making a wide mouth cavity is called:
questions.exp: Debridement: saucerization (wide mouth cavity made). (Book p142)

questions.q: Dead space after debridement is closed with:
questions.exp: Closure of dead space with: bone graft, bone cement. (Book p142)

questions.q: Skin covering after chronic osteomyelitis surgery:
opts: Skin flap, muscle flap or VAC
questions.exp: Skin covering with: skin flap, muscle flap, vacuum assisted covering (VAC). (Book p142)

questions.q: Pressure used in vacuum assisted closure (VAC)/negative pressure wound therapy:
questions.exp: VAC: -75 to -125 mmHg; promotes granulation tissue formation. (Book p142)

questions.q: Vacuum assisted covering promotes:
questions.exp: VAC promotes granulation tissue formation; C/I: eschar tissue or tumor. (Book p142)

questions.q: Contraindication of vacuum assisted covering (VAC):
questions.exp: VAC contraindication: eschar tissue or tumor. (Book p142)

questions.q: Most common complication of chronic osteomyelitis:
questions.exp: Complications: pathological fracture (m/c). (Book p142)

questions.q: Squamous cell carcinoma in chronic osteomyelitis develops due to:
questions.exp: SCC: d/t neoplastic changes of sinus tract. (Book p142)

questions.q: Other complications of chronic osteomyelitis besides pathological fracture and SCC:
questions.exp: Complications: pathological fracture (m/c), acute exacerbation, SCC (sinus tract), amyloidosis. (Book p142)

questions.q: Variants of osteomyelitis (Brodie's/Garre's) show no sinus or sequestrum because:
opts: Good patient immunity + organism of low virulence - infection contained
questions.exp: Pathogenesis: patient has good immunity, organism has low virulence → infection contained; no sinus or sequestrum. (Book p143)

questions.q: Course of Brodie's abscess:
questions.exp: Brodie's abscess: subacute course. (Book p143)

questions.q: Most common site of Brodie's abscess:
questions.exp: Brodie's: m/c site tibia (proximal end). (Book p143)

questions.q: Presence of pus in Brodie's abscess:
questions.exp: Brodie's abscess: pus + (vs Garré's: pus -). (Book p143)

questions.q: Clinical features of Brodie's abscess:
opts: Acute dull aching pain + low grade fever
questions.exp: Clinical: acute dull aching pain, low grade fever; elevated ESR & CRP (+). (Book p143)

questions.q: X-ray of Brodie's abscess shows:
opts: Thick sclerotic rim with central lucency
questions.exp: X-ray: thick sclerotic rim + central lucency. (Book p143)

questions.q: Penumbra sign on MRI - central lucency surrounded by dense sclerotic rim - is seen in:
questions.exp: MRI: penumbra sign - central lucency surrounded by dense sclerotic rim (Brodie's). (Book p143)

questions.q: Treatment of Brodie's abscess:
questions.exp: Rx: antibiotics ± debridement. (Book p143)

questions.q: Course of Garré's sclerosing osteomyelitis:
questions.exp: Garré's sclerosing osteomyelitis: chronic course. (Book p143)

questions.q: Most common site of Garré's sclerosing osteomyelitis:
questions.exp: Garré's: mandible > tibia. (Book p143)

questions.q: Pus in Garré's sclerosing osteomyelitis:
questions.exp: Garré's: pus -; clinical feature: bony swelling; ESR & CRP not elevated (-). (Book p143)

questions.q: X-ray in Garré's sclerosing osteomyelitis shows:
opts: Thick dense bone due to excessive periosteal reaction
questions.exp: X-ray: thick dense bone (d/t excessive periosteal reaction). (Book p143)

questions.q: Treatment of Garré's sclerosing osteomyelitis:
questions.exp: Rx: antibiotics. (Book p143)

questions.q: Septic arthritis is a surgical emergency because:
opts: If pus is not removed from joint immediately - destruction of joint
It always causes septicemia within hours
questions.exp: Surgical emergency: if pus not removed from joint immediately → destruction of joint. (Book p144)

questions.q: Septic arthritis is most common in:
questions.exp: Children (<5 years) > elderly people (relatively low immunity). (Book p144)

questions.q: Most common route of septic arthritis:
questions.exp: Route: m/c hematogenous. (Book p144)

questions.q: Most common organism of septic arthritis:
questions.exp: Organism: m/c Staphylococcus aureus; IV drug abusers: Pseudomonas; sexually active: gonococcus. (Book p144)

questions.q: Organism of septic arthritis in IV drug abusers:
questions.exp: IV drug abusers: Pseudomonas. (Book p144)

questions.q: Organism of septic arthritis in sexually active young patients:
questions.exp: Sexually active: gonococcus. (Book p144)

questions.q: Most common site of septic arthritis:
questions.exp: Site: m/c knee (ends of bone exposed); infants: hip (Tom Smith arthritis). (Book p144)

questions.q: In infants, septic arthritis commonly involves the hip and is called:
questions.exp: Infants: hip (Tom Smith arthritis). (Book p144)

questions.q: Local inflammatory features of septic arthritis:
opts: Swelling, redness, pain (effusion stretches the capsule)
questions.exp: Local inflammatory features: swelling, redness; pain - effusion in joint → capsule stretches (pain sensitive) → no movement at joint. (Book p144)

questions.q: The joint assumes position of ease in septic arthritis to:
opts: Increase joint volume - decrease capsular stretching - decrease pain
questions.exp: Position of ease: increased volume of joint → decreased capsular stretching → decreased pain. (Book p144)

questions.q: Position of ease of the hip in septic arthritis:
questions.exp: Hip - FABER: flexion, abduction, external rotation. (Book p144)

questions.q: Position of ease of the knee in septic arthritis:
questions.exp: Knee: 5-30° flexion. (Book p144)

questions.q: Sign of knee effusion in septic arthritis:
questions.exp: Signs: patellar tap sign +ve. (Book p144)

questions.q: Blood investigations ordered in septic arthritis:
opts: CBC, ESR, CRP, TLC, blood culture
questions.exp: Blood investigations: CBC, ESR, CRP, TLC, blood culture. (Book p144)

questions.q: Early X-ray finding in septic arthritis:
opts: No changes ± widening of joint space
questions.exp: X-ray - early: no changes ± widening of joint space; late: destruction of joint. (Book p144)

questions.q: Late X-ray finding of septic arthritis:
opts: Destruction of joint (bony ankylosis end stage)
questions.exp: X-ray late: destruction of joint; end sequelae - bony ankylosis. (Book p144)

questions.q: MRI in septic arthritis shows:
questions.exp: MRI: synovial thickening. (Book p144)

questions.q: USG-guided arthrocentesis in septic arthritis is:
questions.exp: USG guided arthrocentesis: diagnostic & therapeutic. (Book p144)

questions.q: Treatment of choice of septic arthritis:
opts: Arthrotomy - irrigation & debridement of septic joint contents under antibiotic cover
questions.exp: Arthrotomy (TOC): irrigation & debridement of septic joint contents under antibiotic cover. (Book p145)

questions.q: End sequelae of neglected septic arthritis:
questions.exp: Complication: bony ankylosis - end sequelae of neglected septic arthritis. (Book p145)

questions.q: Organisms in septic arthritis release which proteolytic enzymes?
questions.exp: Organisms release proteolytic enzymes: collagenases, metalloproteinases, elastases. (Book p145)

questions.q: Sequence leading to bony ankylosis in septic arthritis:
opts: Enzymes destroy articular cartilage - raw ends of bone exposed - heal with fusion
questions.exp: Destroy articular cartilage → raw ends of bone exposed → heal with fusion → bony ankylosis. (Book p145)

questions.q: Fusion of bone due to disease process is called:
questions.exp: Ankylosis: fusion d/t disease process; arthrodesis: surgical fusion (eg neglected CTEV → triple arthrodesis). (Book p145)

questions.q: Surgical fusion of a joint is called:
questions.exp: Arthrodesis (surgical fusion); eg neglected CTEV → triple arthrodesis. (Book p145)

questions.q: Bony ankylosis (bony fusion) is caused by:
opts: Pyogenic septic arthritis and TB spine (spondylitis)
questions.exp: Bony: fusion by bone; causes - pyogenic septic arthritis, TB spine (spondylitis). (Book p145)

questions.q: Fibrous ankylosis is typically caused by:
questions.exp: Fibrous: fusion by fibrous tissue; cause - TB arthritis. (Book p145)

questions.q: Regarding movement and pain in bony vs fibrous ankylosis:
opts: Bony: no movement, no pain; fibrous: movement present, pain present
Bony: movement present; fibrous: no movement
questions.exp: Bony ankylosis: movement (-), pain (-), stable; fibrous: movement (+), pain (+), unstable. (Book p145)

questions.q: Stability of joint in bony vs fibrous ankylosis:
questions.exp: Bony ankylosis: stable; fibrous: unstable. (Book p145)

questions.q: Tom Smith arthritis is:
opts: Septic arthritis of hip in infancy (<1 year)
questions.exp: Tom Smith arthritis: septic arthritis of hip in infancy (<1 year); emergency - need immediate intervention to preserve hip function. (Book p145)

questions.q: Pathogenesis of Tom Smith arthritis:
opts: Pus & proteolytic enzymes destroy capital femoral epiphysis - chondrolysis
questions.exp: Disease process (pus & proteolytic enzymes) → destroys capital femoral epiphysis (cartilaginous in children) → chondrolysis. (Book p145)

questions.q: Clinical features of Tom Smith arthritis:
opts: Hypermobility of hip joint, limb shortening, telescopy test +
questions.exp: Clinical: hypermobility of hip joint, limb shortening, telescopy test +ve. (Book p145)

questions.q: Transient synovitis is:
questions.exp: Transient synovitis: self limiting inflammation of synovium; age group 6-12 years. (Book p146)

questions.q: Age group of transient synovitis:
questions.exp: Age group: 6-12 years. (Book p146)

questions.q: Pathogenesis of transient synovitis:
opts: Recent viral infection - antigen antibody reaction - synovitis - increased synovial fluid - capsule stretching - pain
questions.exp: Recent viral infection → Ag-Ab reaction → synovitis → increased synovial fluid production → stretching of capsule → pain. (Book p146)

questions.q: Clinical features of transient synovitis:
opts: Pain, limp, mild fever, position of ease
Complete inability to move limb always
questions.exp: Clinical: pain, limp, mild fever, position of ease. (Book p146)

questions.q: Best investigation to differentiate transient synovitis from septic arthritis:
questions.exp: Aspiration of joint: best investigation to differentiate from septic arthritis; blood: ESR, CRP, TLC. (Book p146)

questions.q: Treatment of transient synovitis:
opts: Observation - hence also called observation hip
questions.exp: Treatment: observation (transient synovitis also called observation hip). (Book p146)

questions.q: Kocher's criteria are used to:
opts: Differentiate between transient synovitis & septic arthritis
questions.exp: Kocher's criteria: to differentiate between transient synovitis & septic arthritis. (Book p146)

questions.q: Kocher's criteria include all except:
opts: Difficulty in weight bearing/unable to walk
questions.exp: Kocher's: difficulty weight bearing/unable to walk, temp >38.5°C (101.3°F), ESR >40 mm/hr, WBC >12,000 cells/mm³ - each has 1 point. (Book p146)

questions.q: Interpretation of Kocher's criteria:
opts: Each criterion has 1 point - more points → more chance of septic arthritis
Each has 2 points - fewer points → septic arthritis
questions.exp: Each criterion has 1 point; increased point → increased chance of septic arthritis. (Book p146)

questions.q: Most common cause of limp in a child:
opts: Transient synovitis > septic arthritis > Perthe's disease
questions.exp: Cause of limp in child: transient synovitis (m/c) > septic arthritis > Perthe's disease. (Book p146)

questions.q: Paronychia is also known as:
questions.exp: Paronychia (running around the nail): m/c infection of hand. (Book p146)

questions.q: Most common infection of the hand:
questions.exp: Paronychia: m/c infection of hand; infection around the nail and nail bed. (Book p146)

questions.q: Most common organism of paronychia:
questions.exp: m/c organism: Staphylococcus aureus. (Book p146)

questions.q: Treatment of paronychia:
opts: Antibiotics + drainage of abscess + removal of part of nail (if infection reaches nail bed)
questions.exp: Treatment: antibiotics + drainage of abscess + removal of part of nail (if infection reaches nail bed). (Book p147)

questions.q: Felon/whitlow is infection of:
opts: Subcutaneous tissue (pulp) of the finger - distal phalanx
questions.exp: Felon/whitlow: infection of subcutaneous tissue (pulp) of the finger (distal phalanx). (Book p147)

questions.q: Most common finger affected in felon:
questions.exp: Finger affected: thumb (m/c) > index finger; m/c organism: Staphylococcus aureus. (Book p147)

questions.q: Complications of felon:
questions.exp: Complications: osteomyelitis of phalanx, tenosynovitis. (Book p147)

questions.q: Incision used in felon drainage:
opts: Vertical incision - to break adhesions/septae that hide infection
questions.exp: Treatment: antibiotics + incision (vertical incision to break adhesions/septae that hide infection) & drainage. (Book p147)

questions.q: Tenosynovitis is infection of:
questions.exp: Tenosynovitis: infection of tendon/tendon sheath; m/c organism: Staphylococcus aureus. (Book p147)

questions.q: Symptoms of tenosynovitis include:
opts: Fever, flexion attitude, fusiform swelling of fingers, pain on passive extension
questions.exp: Symptoms: fever, flexion attitude, fusiform swelling of fingers, pain on passive extension. (Book p147)

questions.q: Kanavel sign is:
opts: Pain on tapping the affected tendon (+ve in tenosynovitis)
questions.exp: Signs: Kanavel sign +ve - pain on tapping affected tendon. (Book p147)

questions.q: Treatment of tenosynovitis:
questions.exp: Treatment: antibiotics + incision & drainage. (Book p147)

units.title: Sequestrum
units.guide: A dead, dense, devascularized island of bone floating in pus, wrapped in granulation tissue and involucrum, its haversian systems destroyed - the pathological signature of chronicity.

units.title: Types of Sequestrum
units.guide: Shape names the disease: coral for Perthe's, ring for pins and stumps, tubular for pyogenic infection, feathery sandy for TB, fine sandy for viral, button-hole after radiation, ivory for syphilis.

units.title: Chronic OM: Workup & Initial Rx
units.guide: X-ray unmasks sequestrum, involucrum and cloaca; dye through the sinus maps its track; biopsy remains gold standard - start broad-spectrum antibiotics and support the patient.

units.title: Surgery for Chronic OM
units.guide: The operative ladder under antibiotic cover: sequestrectomy, curettage to the Paprika blush, saucerization, dead space filled with graft or cement, skin flapped or VAC'd at -75 to -125 mmHg - never on eschar or tumor.

units.title: Chronic OM Complications
units.guide: Pathological fracture comes first, sinuses can turn squamous, and flare-ups and amyloidosis round out the toll of a chronic discharging wound.

units.title: Variants & Brodie's Abscess
units.guide: Strong host, weak bug - infection walled off without sinus or sequestrum. Brodie's: subacute, proximal tibia, pus positive, dull ache with low fever, a lucent eye ringed by sclerotic rim - penumbra on MRI - treat with antibiotics ± debridement.

units.title: Garre's Sclerosing OM
units.guide: Garré's: the dry chronic twin - mandible more than tibia, no pus, no raised ESR, just bony hard swelling and bone gone rock-dense from excessive periosteal reaction; antibiotics suffice.

units.title: Septic Arthritis: Basics
units.guide: Pus in a joint is a surgical emergency - undrained it digests cartilage. Under-five children and the elderly, blood-borne Staph aureus (Pseudomonas in addicts, gonococcus in the sexually active), knee first, hip in infants - Tom Smith.

units.title: Septic Arthritis: Clinical
units.guide: Swollen, red, exquisitely painful joint held still; the limb rests where the capsule is slackest - hip in FABER, knee at 5-30 degrees - and the knee offers a positive patellar tap.

units.title: Septic Arthritis: Investigations
units.guide: Bloods and culture, an early film that shows little but a widened space, late destruction, MRI synovial thickening - and ultrasound-guided arthrocentesis that both names the culprit and relieves the joint.

units.title: Rx & Ankylosis Types
units.guide: Arthrotomy with irrigation and debridement is TOC; neglect lets collagenases strip cartilage until raw bones fuse - bony ankylosis. Disease fusion is ankylosis (bony from pyogenic/TB spine - stable, painless; fibrous from TB - mobile, painful, unstable), surgery's is arthrodesis.

units.title: Tom Smith Arthritis
units.guide: Infant's septic hip under one year: pus and enzymes dissolve the cartilaginous capital epiphysis - chondrolysis - leaving a hypermobile, shortened limb with positive telescopy.

units.title: Transient Synovitis & Kocher's
units.guide: A post-viral, self-limiting 'observation hip' of 6-12 year olds: limp, mild fever, position of ease. Joint aspiration is the best divider, Kocher counts four points - weight bearing, >38.5°C, ESR >40, WBC >12,000 - the more, the more septic. Limp in a child: transient synovitis first.

units.title: Paronychia
units.guide: The commonest hand infection runs around the nail - Staph aureus again; drain it, and if it sneaks under the nail bed, lift a piece of nail.

units.title: Felon (Whitlow)
units.guide: Pulp-space abscess of the distal phalanx, thumb first: a tense throbbing digit that can erode into bone or tendon; a vertical incision breaks the septae and lets the pus go.

units.title: Tenosynovitis
units.guide: Infected tendon sheath: finger held flexed, fusiform swelling, pain on passive extension and Kanavel's tap - antibiotics plus incision and drainage.
